match-whole-word.context: The letters a and b between square brackets with a line under them. It is the whole word option in find and replace bars and code editor search boxes.

paste-as-text.context: A clipboard with a capital T on its sheet. Used for commands that paste copied content without its fonts, colours or links.

clipboard-history.context: A clipboard with a small clock at its lower corner. Used for lists of recently copied items that can be pasted again.

insert-symbol.context: An omega sign inside a rounded square. It stands for the command that opens a special character picker in editors.

insert-equation.context: A pi sign beside an equals mark inside a rounded square. Used for commands that add a maths formula to a document.

autosave.context: A document with a circular arrow and a small cloud at its corner. Shows that changes are being saved automatically.

ruby-annotation.context: A large East Asian style character with a row of tiny marks above it. Used for pronunciation guides written above characters in Japanese, Chinese and Korean text.

emphasis-dots.context: Three character marks in a row, each with a small dot above it. Marks emphasis in East Asian text the way italics do in Latin text.

kashida-justification.context: A flowing cursive stroke with a double arrow stretching above its middle. Stands for Arabic style justification that lengthens connecting strokes instead of widening spaces.

bidirectional-text.context: Two lines of text, one with an arrow pointing right and one with an arrow pointing left. Shows text that mixes left to right and right to left scripts.

boustrophedon.context: A path that runs along a line, turns around and returns along the next line, ending in an arrow. It shows the ancient practice of writing alternate lines in opposite directions.

phonetic-transcription.context: A schwa sign between two slashes. It is how pronunciation is written in dictionaries and linguistics papers.

transliteration.context: A Latin letter A, an arrow and a Cyrillic letter Ya. Used for converting text from one alphabet to another by sound.

enclosed-character.context: A letter A inside a circle with a second circle overlapping behind it. Used for circled letters, badge style initials and enclosed alphanumerics.

dyslexia-friendly-text.context: The letters b and d with weighted bottoms standing on a thick baseline. Marks fonts and reading modes designed to keep mirror like letters apart.

typing-speed.context: A keyboard with a small speedometer dial above it. Used for typing tests and words per minute results.

grease-pencil.context: A marking pencil with a spiral paper wrapper and a peeled tip. Used for pencils that write on glass, film and glossy surfaces.

typewriter-eraser.context: A pencil shaped eraser with a round rubber end and a small brush at the other end. A traditional tool for correcting typed pages.

pica-ruler.context: A straight ruler with long and short marks along its edge and small blocks for point sizes. Used by designers and printers to measure type and line length.

linen-tester.context: A small square lens on a folding stand above a flat base. Used to inspect printed dots, fabric weave and photographs up close.

printers-chase.context: A rectangular metal frame with a crossbar, lines of type on one side and locking wedges on the other. The frame that holds type in place on a letterpress.

type-slug.context: A long metal bar with a row of raised letters cast along its top edge. Made by line casting machines for hot metal printing.

dry-transfer-lettering.context: A sheet printed with a letter A and a pencil rubbing over it. Stands for rub down lettering that is pressed onto artwork by hand.

proof-press.context: A flat bed press with a large roller held above the bed by two posts and turned with a hand crank. Used to pull proofs from set type.

book-chapter.context: An open book with a large numeral 1 and a text line on the left page and text lines on the right. Marks the start of a chapter.

ghostwriter.context: A small ghost holding a pen that writes a line. Stands for writing done by someone who is not credited.

digital-notepad.context: A thin tablet with handwritten lines on its screen and a stylus resting on it. Used for handwriting and note taking apps.

letter-stamps.context: Two small rubber stamps with round handles and the letters T and A on their bases. Used for alphabet stamp sets in crafts and printing.

calligraphy-guide-sheet.context: A sheet crossed by horizontal ruled lines and evenly spaced slanted lines. Used under practice paper to keep lettering height and slant steady.

didone-font.context: A capital A with a heavy right stroke, a hairline left stroke and thin flat serifs. Shows high contrast modern serif type.

seven-segment-digits.context: A figure eight built from seven separate bars. The shape of numbers on calculators, clocks and meters.

letter-aperture.context: A lowercase c with three dots marking the gap between its two ends. Shows the opening of a letter, a trait that affects how easy type is to read.

side-bearings.context: A letter n inside a box with the empty strips on its left and right marked off. Used in font editors to set the space on each side of a glyph.

cjk-full-stop.context: Two character marks followed by a small hollow circle sitting at the baseline. Shows the ideographic full stop that ends sentences in Chinese and Japanese.

eyebrow-heading.context: A short line of small spaced text above a thick heading bar and two lines of body text. Shows the small label that sits over a title.

shape-poem.context: Short lines of text growing wider row by row to make the outline of a tree. Stands for poems and text art laid out in the shape of their subject.

palimpsest.context: A page with bold lines of text over dashed traces of older writing. Used for manuscripts that were scraped and reused, and for layered or overwritten text.

underline-skip-ink.context: The letters g and y with an underline that breaks where their tails cross it. Shows the text decoration setting that keeps lines from touching descenders.

hook-above-accent.context: A lowercase a with a small question mark shaped hook above it. Used for the hook above tone mark in Vietnamese and similar writing.

typewriter-key.context: A round typewriter key with a letter on its face, standing on a neck above a slanted lever arm. Stands for manual typewriters and vintage typing.

proportion-wheel.context: Two stacked round discs with a ring of scale marks and a small window at the middle. A paste up tool for working out how much to enlarge or shrink a picture.

ornamental-rule.context: A horizontal line with a small diamond and two curling flourishes at its centre. Used as a decorative divider between sections of text.

ai-writing-assistant.context: A pen nib writing a line beside a four point sparkle. Used for tools that draft or improve text with artificial intelligence.

paragraph-shading.context: Text lines above and below a hatched band. Stands for the setting that gives a paragraph a coloured background.

paragraph-border.context: A block of text lines inside a thin rectangular outline. Stands for the setting that draws a box around a paragraph.

table-of-authorities.context: A page with citation rows ending in page numbers and a small gavel at its lower corner. Used for the list of cases and statutes at the front of a legal brief.

handwritten-markup.context: A page with text lines, a hand drawn loop and an arrow leading out to the margin. Used for proofreading marks and review comments.

synchronized-scrolling.context: Two narrow document pages with a pair of vertical arrows linking them. Used when two panes scroll together in a compare view.

synced-block.context: Two content blocks stacked on the left with circular sync arrows on their right. Stands for a block of content that stays identical wherever it appears.

master-page.context: A page in front of a second page behind it, with the letter A on the front page. Used for page templates whose items repeat on other pages.

page-construction-canon.context: Two facing pages each crossed by diagonal lines with a small text block at the crossing. Shows the classic geometric method for placing margins and the text area.

comic-sound-effect.context: A jagged burst with a bold slanted letter inside. Used for action words and sound effects in comics and graphic novels.

acronym.context: Three stacked words whose first letters are drawn larger and bold in a column. Shows how an acronym is spelled out from initial letters.

replacement-character.context: A diamond with a question mark inside. The mark shown when software cannot display a character, often from a text encoding error.

interlinear-translation.context: Bold lines of text each with a dotted smaller line directly beneath it. Used for word by word glosses and translations set between lines.

parallel-text.context: An open book with the letter A on the left page and a Cyrillic letter on the right, each above a text line. Stands for books that print two languages side by side.

scansion-marks.context: A row of short syllable bars with alternating breve and stress marks above them. Used to mark the rhythm of lines of verse.

typewriter-typeball.context: A sphere covered in raised character bumps with a clip at its top. The swappable print head used by some electric typewriters.

fluid-typography.context: A small phone beside a wide monitor, the monitor showing a larger letter A. Stands for text that scales smoothly with screen width.

code-ligature.context: An equals sign and a greater than sign above a merged double arrow. Shows a programming font joining symbol pairs into one arrow.

postscript-note.context: A letter page with a signature scribble and a short extra line below it led by two small marks. Stands for the P.S. added after a signature.

spoiler-text.context: Lines of text with a speckled hidden block covering part of the middle line. Used for text that stays hidden until clicked.

backlinks.context: Two note pages with a bent arrow running from the lower page back up to the upper one. Shows the list of pages that link to the current note.

diacritic-anchor.context: A lowercase a with a small crosshair above it. Marks the point where an accent attaches in font design.

horizontal-in-vertical-text.context: A vertical column of character boxes with two small digits set side by side in the middle. Shows upright numbers inside vertical East Asian text.

erasing-shield.context: A thin flat plate pierced with a round hole, a narrow slot and a square opening. A drafting tool that limits an eraser to one small area.
